notes: Policy the bash-guard MCP server applies to every Bash command the box's
Claude Code is about to run. First matching rule wins, so order matters:
specific denies come before the broader asks that would also match.
Patterns are Python regexes, searched (not anchored) against the raw
command string unless the pattern anchors itself. [^;&|]* is used instead
of .* so a pattern cannot span a shell separator and match fragments of
two unrelated commands in one chain.
Decisions: deny blocks and tells Claude why; ask prompts the user; allow
skips the permission prompt; undecided (the default) stays silent and
lets Claude Code's own permission flow decide. Edit and save this file to
change policy — the server reloads it on the next call, no restart.
These are heuristics against accidents, not a security boundary: anything
that can write to this file or encode a command past a regex is out of

rules.reason: Refusing to delete a filesystem root, the home directory, or the whole /workspace mount. Delete a specific subdirectory instead.
Refusing to format or raw-write a block device from inside the box.
Refusing to run a fork bomb.
This reads a private key or stored credential. Confirm you want its contents in the transcript.
This pipes a downloaded script straight into a shell. Confirm the source is one you trust.
This runs as root inside the box.
This powers off or reboots the box, ending the session.
This deletes a directory tree. Check the path before confirming.
This rewrites history on the remote.
This publishes commits to a remote.
This changes state on GitHub, visible to other people.
